## § 01_GLYPHS.csl

```
§ PRIMITIVE SIGIL TABLE
R! ← Iverson (APL): 1 glyph = 1 op • tokenizer-aligned
R! ← Egyptian determinatives: type-marker glyphs carry 0 phonetics, pure semantic
R! ← Peirce Alpha: ¬ = enclosure

§ STRUCTURAL (flow/scope)
§     → section header (replaces #, ##, ###; depth = count)
→     → then / yields / maps-to
←     → from / sourced / derives
↔     → bidirectional / isomorphic
⇒     → implies (logical)
⊢     → entails / proves
∴     → therefore
∵     → because
∎     → QED / block-end

§ QUANTITATIVE (status/cert)
✓     → confirmed / true / done
◐     → partial / in-progress
○     → pending / unknown
✗     → failed / false / blocked
!     → urgent / assert
?     → query / uncertain
~     → approximate
≈     → roughly-equal

§ MODAL (must/may/should)
W!    → MUST (hard requirement)
R!    → SHOULD (strong recommend)
M?    → MAY (optional)
N!    → MUST NOT
I>    → INSIGHT / key claim
Q?    → QUESTION

§ SET/LOGIC (Peirce Beta + std)
∀     → for all
∃     → exists
∈     → member-of
∉     → not-member
∪ ∩   → union / intersect
⊂ ⊃   → subset / superset
¬     → not (Peirce enclosure fallback)
∧ ∨   → and / or
⊕     → xor

§ REFERENCE (Sanskrit samasa markers)
§X    → section X reference
@X    → anchor/label X
#X    → tag X
&X    → alias X
*X    → pointer to X (compiler: indirect)
$X    → variable/slot X

§ TYPE (Egyptian determinative pattern)
:T    → postfix type annotation
::K   → kind annotation (type-of-type)
 ʈ    → trait/interface marker
 ɴ    → numeric class
 ꜱ    → string/symbol class
 ʙ    → bool class
 ᴠ    → vector/array class
 ᴍ    → map/assoc class

§ TEMPORAL
t→    → future
t←    → past
t=    → now
t∞    → eternal/invariant
Δ     → change / delta
∂     → partial-derivative / local-change

§ RELATION
~>    → causes / triggers
|>    → pipeline / forward-compose
<|    → backward-compose
>>    → dispatch / send
<<    → receive / consume
⟨ ⟩   → tuple / record
⟦ ⟧   → semantic brackets (meaning-of)
```

## § 02_GRAMMAR.csl

```
§ SURFACE SYNTAX
R! ← J lang: ASCII fallback everywhere • glyph+ASCII alias table
R! ← Lojban: unambiguous parse via rigid word-class markers

§ TOKEN CLASSES
GLYPH   → single unicode sigil (table §01)
WORD    → [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]* (identifiers, densified nouns)
NUM     → integer, float, hex (0x), bin (0b)
STR     → "..." or `...` (raw)
CSL     → CSL-in-CSL meta-quote

§ LINE STRUCTURE (Caveman rule)
DROP:  articles (a/an/the), auxiliaries (is/are/was), copulas where inferable, filler (that/which)
KEEP:  nouns, verbs, relationships, numbers, gates, glyphs
ORDER: topic → relation → object • SVO collapse when unambiguous

§ BLOCK STRUCTURE
§ HEADER
  content
  content
∎  § optional explicit close; indentation-sensitive otherwise

§ STATEMENT FORMS
  X → Y                 § X yields Y
  X :T                  § X has type T
  X W! cond             § X must satisfy cond
  X ∈ {a,b,c}           § membership
  ∀x∈S: P(x)            § quantified
  [x |> f |> g]         § pipeline
  ⟨k=v, k=v⟩            § record literal

§ PARSE PRIORITY (high→low)
  glyph-prefix (§ @ # & * $)
  enclosure  ( ) [ ] { } ⟨ ⟩ ⟦ ⟧
  unary      ¬ ~ !
  binary-tight  : :: .
  binary-arith  * / %  +  -
  binary-cmp   < > ≤ ≥ = ≠ ≈
  binary-logic ∧ ∨ ⊕
  binary-flow  → ← ⇒ ↔ |> <|
  binary-meta  ⊢ ∴ ∵ ~>

§ AMBIGUITY RULE
W! ∄ ambiguous parse • if two readings: mandatory explicit grouping
R! LL(2) target • parseable w/ 2-token lookahead
```

## § 03_MORPH.csl

```
§ COMPOUND FORMATION
R! ← Sanskrit samasa: arbitrary-depth nominal compounds w/ explicit relation
R! ← Ithkuil: 96 grammatical slots per word via morpheme stacking
R! ← German: head-final, modifier-chains

§ FOUR COMPOUND CLASSES (from Sanskrit)
DV (dvandva)      → A+B = {A, B}        coordinate; A,B co-equal
TP (tatpurusha)   → A+B = B_of_A        dependent; A modifies/qualifies B
BV (bahuvrihi)    → A+B = thing_having_AB  exocentric; refers outside
AV (avyayibhava)  → A+B = adverbial_AB  relational; indeclinable result

§ CSL ENCODING
A·B     → TP (head=B, mod=A)  [default, most common]
A+B     → DV (coord)
A⊗B     → BV (exocentric, "that which has A and B")
A°B     → AV (adverbial)

§ EXAMPLES
voxel·engine       → TP: engine of-voxels
render·pipe·stage  → TP chain: stage of-pipe of-render (right-head)
cpu+gpu            → DV: both CPU and GPU
red⊗crown          → BV: entity having red crown
fast°render        → AV: rendered fast-ly

§ MORPHEME STACKING (Ithkuil-inspired)
R! suffix stack encodes aspect/modality/cert/scope
BASE[.aspect][.mod][.cert][.scope]
  aspect: .prog .perf .iter .hab .inch .term
  mod:    .must .may .cant .will .won
  cert:   .cert .prob .poss .doubt
  scope:  .loc .glob .ctx

§ EX
render.prog.cert     → is-definitely-rendering
spawn.iter.may.loc   → may-repeatedly-spawn, locally
merge.inch.must      → must-begin-merging

§ DENSITY BOUND
I> avg Ithkuil morpheme ≈ 4.5 bits semantic content
I> avg EN word ≈ 11 bits surface, ≈ 2.8 bits semantic (Shannon)
I> CSLv2 target ≈ 6-8 bits semantic/token (tokenizer-measured)
```

## § 04_SPATIAL.csl

```
§ 2D OPERATORS
R! ← Peirce Existential Graphs: enclosure = negation, juxtaposition = conjunction
R! ← Penrose/tensor diagrams: spatial = structural
R! ← Feynman: time-axis implicit in layout

§ ENCLOSURE SEMANTICS
( X )           → grouping
[ X ]           → list/seq
{ X }           → set/block
⟨ X ⟩           → tuple/record
⟦ X ⟧           → meaning/semantic-of
« X »           → quotation (X is mentioned, not used)
⌈ X ⌉           → ceiling / upper-bound / invariant
⌊ X ⌋           → floor / lower-bound / precondition

§ PEIRCE ENCLOSURE → NEGATION (optional mode)
¬(X)    ≡ ⦇ X ⦈
double-cut: ⦇ ⦇ X ⦈ ⦈ = X    § Peirce rule of insertion/erasure

§ TENSOR/STRING DIAGRAMS (ASCII form)
  X ─f→ Y ─g→ Z        § f:X→Y, g:Y→Z, sequential
  X ═╗
      ╠ h → W           § h: X⊗Y → W, parallel inputs
  Y ═╝

§ DATAFLOW (Feynman-style, for agent reasoning)
  vertical = time
  horizontal = parallel computation
  labels on edges = typed values
  vertices = ops
  
  use in §05 (REASON) blocks when causal structure > linear prose

§ TABLES (2D as pure information)
| col1 | col2 | col3 |
|------|------|------|
| ...  | ...  | ...  |
R! use when data is genuinely 2D; DON'T linearize tables into prose
```

## § 06_SPEC.csl

```
§ SPEC-WRITING CONVENTIONS
W! specs are implementation-ready • no hedging, no prose filler
R! every spec has: §GOAL §DATA §OPS §INVARIANTS §TESTS §ANTI

§ STANDARD SPEC TEMPLATE
§ <NAME>.spec
§ GOAL
  what:  ⟨one-line⟩
  why:   ⟨one-line⟩
  
§ DATA
  struct X ⟨
    field :T  § comment-if-needed
    ...
  ⟩
  
§ OPS
  op₁ : X → Y
    pre:   ⌊cond⌋
    post:  ⌈cond⌉
    body:  ⟨CSL or target-lang code⟩
    
§ INVARIANTS
  t∞: ∀x∈X: P(x)
  
§ TESTS
  case₁: input → expected ✓
  case₂: input → expected ✓
  edge:  boundary → behavior ✓
  
§ ANTI-PATTERNS
  ✗ don't: ⟨pattern⟩ ∵ ⟨reason⟩
  ✓ do:    ⟨alt⟩
∎

§ DENSITY RULES
DROP: "In order to", "It is important to", "Note that", "Please"
DROP: "will be", "can be", "should be" → use W! R! M?
DROP: restatement-of-header in first sentence
KEEP: numbers, formulas, code, types
REPLACE: "because" → ∵ • "therefore" → ∴ • "such that" → ⊢

§ CODE EMBEDDING
CSL specs embed target-lang code in fenced blocks:
  ```rust
  fn foo(x: u32) -> u32 { x * 2 }
  ```
CSL surrounds; code is literal.
```

## § 07_CSSL2.csl

```
§ CSSL2 COMPILER FRONTEND
I> CSSL2 = programming language; ingests CSL-native source
I> CSL = notation; CSSL2 = executable subset of CSL
R! ← Forth/Factor: stack-based, concatenative
R! ← APL: rank-polymorphic operators
R! ← Agda: dependent types as specs

§ LEXICAL
token ← glyph | word | num | str | punct
whitespace = separator (except in strings)
comments: § ... EOL  OR  §{ ... §}

§ CORE FORMS
decl     : name : type = expr
fn-def   : name ⟨params⟩ → ret = body
type-def : type name = ⟨fields⟩ | variant | ...
import   : use §module.name
export   : pub name

§ EXPRESSION GRAMMAR (CFG sketch)
expr    ::= atom | unary | binary | call | lambda | pipeline | block
atom    ::= num | str | ident | glyph-literal
unary   ::= (¬|~|!|-) expr
binary  ::= expr op expr
call    ::= expr ⟨args⟩
lambda  ::= λ ⟨params⟩ → expr
pipeline::= expr (|> expr)+
block   ::= { stmt* expr? }

§ TYPE SYSTEM
primitives: ɴ{8,16,32,64}, ꜱ, ʙ, ᴠ⟨T⟩, ᴍ⟨K,V⟩
algebraic:  sum ( T₁ | T₂ | ... ), product ⟨f₁:T₁, f₂:T₂⟩
dependent:  Π⟨x:T⟩ → U(x)     § pi (for-all type)
            Σ⟨x:T, y:U(x)⟩    § sigma (exists type)
refinement: { x:T ⊢ P(x) }    § subset type
linear:     T!                § must-use-once
shared:     T&                § borrowed ref

§ BACKEND TARGETS
target₁: x86-64 (SysV ABI, AVX2 min; NO AVX-512 — hw constraint §mantle)
target₂: SPIR-V (Vulkan 1.3, compute+graphics)
IR:      SSA + regions (like MLIR); lowering passes per target

§ RANK POLYMORPHISM (APL-inherit)
scalar op: f : T → T
elevated:  f : ᴠ⟨T⟩ → ᴠ⟨T⟩  § auto-lifted
rank-k:    f : ᴠᵏ⟨T⟩ → ᴠᵏ⟨T⟩
R! ops broadcast like numpy; explicit rank annotation when ambiguous

§ EXAMPLE
§ vec-add.cssl2
pub fn add ⟨a: ᴠ⟨ɴ32⟩, b: ᴠ⟨ɴ32⟩⟩ → ᴠ⟨ɴ32⟩ =
  W! |a| = |b|
  a ⊕ b    § elementwise, rank-lifted

§ main
let x = [1,2,3,4] :ᴠ⟨ɴ32⟩
let y = [10,20,30,40]
let z = add⟨x, y⟩
§ z = [11,22,33,44]
∎
```

## § 08_BRIDGE.csl

```
§ EN ↔ CSL TRANSLATION
R! used for: onboarding humans, interop w/ non-CSL tooling, doc gen

§ EN → CSL RULES (compression)
"A is a B"              → A :B
"A must B"              → A W! B
"A should B"            → A R! B  
"A may B"               → A M? B
"If X then Y"           → X ⇒ Y
"X because Y"           → X ∵ Y
"Therefore X"           → ∴ X
"X causes Y"            → X ~> Y
"X yields Y"            → X → Y
"X, Y, and Z"           → [X, Y, Z]
"all X are Y"           → ∀x∈X: x :Y
"there exists X..."     → ∃x: ...
"X of Y"                → Y·X     § right-head compound
"not X"                 → ¬X
"X and Y"               → X ∧ Y
"X or Y"                → X ∨ Y
"is equivalent to"      → ↔
"maps to"               → →
"pre-condition"         → ⌊ ⌋
"post-condition"        → ⌈ ⌉
"invariant"             → t∞:

§ CSL → EN RULES (expansion, for docs)
inverse of above • render for humans unfamiliar w/ CSL

§ MIXED MODE (readable spec)
allow EN sentences surrounded by CSL structure when:
  • explaining rationale to mixed-audience
  • onboarding docs
  • external APIs
W! core spec body always pure CSL

§ EXAMPLE TRANSLATION
EN: "The render pipeline should batch draw calls by material, because GPU 
     state changes are expensive. This must happen before frustum culling."
CSL: render·pipe R! batch·draws ← material
     ∵ gpu·state·Δ = expensive
     W! order: batch ≺ frustum·cull
```

## § 09_EVAL.csl

```
§ COMPRESSION BOUNDS & VALIDATION

§ INFORMATION-THEORETIC TARGET
R! ← Shannon: H(EN prose) ≈ 1.3 bits/char
R! ← Kolmogorov: min description length = theoretical floor
I> EN specs avg 4.7 chars/token (BPE); 1.3 bpc × 4.7 = 6.1 bits/token semantic

MEASURE: CSL bits/token via same BPE
TARGET:  ≥ 2× EN semantic density (≥ 12 bits/token effective info)
METHOD:  encode N test-specs in EN + CSL; compare (token count × perplexity-to-LLM)

§ TEST CORPUS
C1: spec of sorting algorithm       § small, algorithmic
C2: spec of voxel chunk system      § medium, systems
C3: spec of type inference rules    § large, formal
C4: agent CoT trace                 § reasoning substrate
C5: mixed natural-language spec     § bridge/translation

§ METRICS
m₁: token-count(CSL) / token-count(EN)    W! < 0.5
m₂: LLM-perplexity preserving             W! Δ < 10%
m₃: human-parse time (trained reader)     R! < 1.5× EN
m₄: parse-error rate                      W! < EN baseline
m₅: round-trip fidelity (EN→CSL→EN)       R! > 0.95 semantic-sim

§ KNOWN RISKS
⚠ tokenizer-hostile glyphs → some unicode = many tokens
  mitigation: ASCII-alias table (§10); measure per-glyph cost; prune expensive
⚠ agent-drift → LLM may "translate back" to EN internally
  mitigation: prompt R! "reason in CSL"; reinforce via system-prompt
⚠ over-compression → lossy
  mitigation: m₅ round-trip test; flag semantic loss > 5%

§ CONTINUOUS EVAL
every spec written in CSL → run metrics → log
quarterly: prune glyphs w/ cost > benefit
```
